Synopsis:
UK farming bodies and animal health experts are urging a ban on Brazilian meat imports due to antibiotic resistance (AMR) concerns. The EU is implementing such a ban imminently, but the UK has not followed suit. With the EU market closing to Brazilian meat, trade diversion toward the UK is a near-term risk. The issue intersects with food safety, post-Brexit regulatory divergence, Northern Ireland protocol complications, and UK-EU trade realignment politics.
